title: The Book of Genesis Timeline
sub: Creation to Egypt · The Founding Story
desc: From six days of creation through the fall, the flood, and the tower of Babel, Genesis narrows to one family — Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and Joseph — carrying a promise of land, descendants, and blessing all the way down into Egypt.

eras.label: Era One · Genesis 1
eras.name: Six Days of Creation
eras.dates: God speaks the cosmos into being in six structured days — light, sky, land and vegetation, sun and moon and stars, sea and air creatures, land animals and humankind — declaring each stage good and the whole "very good."

events.title: Light, Sky, and Land in Three Days
events.detail: God creates light and separates it from darkness, forms the sky to divide the waters, and gathers the waters to let dry land and vegetation appear — the first three days establishing the world's basic structure.

verses.text: “In the beginning God [Elohim] created the heavens and the earth.”

events.title: Sun, Moon, Stars, and Living Creatures
events.detail: God fills what the first three days structured — lights in the sky to govern day and night and mark seasons, then sea creatures, birds, and land animals, each "according to their kinds."

events.title: Humankind in God's Image
events.detail: God creates humankind, male and female, in his own image, blesses them with authority over the earth's creatures, and declares the completed creation "very good."

verses.text: “Then God [Elohim] said, ‘Let us make humankind in our image, after our likeness…’ God [Elohim] created humankind in his own image, in the image of God [Elohim] he created them, male and female he created them.”

eras.label: Era Two · Genesis 2
eras.name: The Garden of Eden
eras.dates: The narrative slows to a close-up: God forms the man from dust and breathes life into him, plants a garden with two significant trees, and creates the woman as the man's true counterpart out of his own side.

events.title: The Seventh Day, and a Watered Earth
events.detail: God rests on the seventh day and blesses it as holy, and the narrative pauses to describe the earth before humanity's cultivation — watered not by rain but by springs welling up from the ground.

events.title: The Man Formed, and Two Trees in the Garden
events.detail: The LORD God forms the man from soil and breathes life into him, plants an orchard in Eden with the tree of life and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil at its center, and commands him freely to eat from every tree but that one.

verses.text: “The LORD [Yahweh] God [Elohim] formed the man from the soil of the ground and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life, and the man became a living being.”

events.title: "Bone of My Bones" — the Woman Formed
events.detail: Finding no suitable companion among the animals the man names, the LORD God causes him to sleep and forms the woman from his side; the man recognizes her instantly as his own kind, and the two are naked without shame.

verses.text: “The LORD [Yahweh] God [Elohim] said, ‘It is not good for the man to be alone. I will make a companion for him who corresponds to him.’”

eras.label: Era Three · Genesis 3
eras.name: The Fall
eras.dates: A shrewd serpent's question unravels the one prohibition in Eden, and the consequences ripple outward — shame, blame, a curse on the serpent and the ground, and expulsion from the garden.

events.title: The Serpent's Question, and the Forbidden Fruit
events.detail: The serpent convinces the woman that eating the forbidden fruit will make her like God rather than kill her; she eats and gives some to her husband, and their eyes open immediately to their own nakedness.

events.title: "Where Are You?"
events.detail: The man and woman hide from the LORD God's approach; when confronted, the man blames the woman and, implicitly, God himself for giving her to him, and the woman blames the serpent.

verses.text: “The man and his wife heard the sound of the LORD [Yahweh] God [Elohim] moving about in the orchard… and they hid. But the LORD [Yahweh] God [Elohim] called to the man and said to him, ‘Where are you?’”

events.title: Curses, a Promise, and Expulsion From Eden
events.detail: The LORD God curses the serpent to crawl on its belly, promises hostility between the serpent's offspring and the woman's — with the woman's offspring eventually crushing the serpent's head — increases the woman's labor pains, curses the ground for the man's sake, and expels them both from the garden.

verses.text: “I will put hostility between you and the woman and between your offspring and her offspring; he will strike your head, and you will strike his heel.”

eras.label: Era Four · Genesis 4
eras.name: Cain and Abel
eras.dates: The first children born outside Eden bring the first murder — a rejected offering, a warning about sin "crouching at the door," and a brother's blood crying out from the ground.

events.title: Two Offerings, and the First Murder
events.detail: Cain's offering is rejected while Abel's is accepted; despite the LORD's warning that sin desires to dominate him, Cain lures Abel into a field and kills him.

verses.text: “Is it not true that if you do what is right, you will be fine? But if you do not do what is right, sin is crouching at the door. It desires to dominate you, but you must subdue it.”

events.title: "Am I My Brother's Guardian?"
events.detail: The LORD confronts Cain, who deflects the question of Abel's whereabouts before being banished as a wanderer — though marked for protection from being killed himself.

verses.text: “The LORD [Yahweh] said to Cain, ‘Where is your brother Abel?’ And he replied, ‘I don't know! Am I my brother's guardian?’ But the LORD [Yahweh] said, ‘What have you done? The voice of your brother's blood is crying out to me from the ground!’”

events.title: Cain's Line, and the Beginning of Worship
events.detail: Cain's descendants build cities and develop tools, music, and metalworking, while Lamech's boast of disproportionate vengeance escalates the violence Cain began; the chapter closes with Seth's line and the note that "people began to worship the LORD" by name.

verses.text: “A son was also born to Seth, whom he named Enosh. At that time people began to worship the LORD [Yahweh].”

eras.label: Era Five · Genesis 5
eras.name: From Adam to Noah
eras.dates: A genealogy measured entirely in centuries carries the human story from Adam to Noah, broken only by one striking exception — Enoch, who simply "walked with God" until he was no more.

events.title: Adam to Jared
events.detail: The genealogy from Adam through Seth, Enosh, Kenan, Mahalalel, and Jared records each man's age at fatherhood and death, spanning centuries with each generation.

events.title: Enoch Walked With God
events.detail: Unlike every other name in the genealogy, Enoch's entry breaks the pattern entirely — no age at death, only that he "walked with God, and then he disappeared because God took him away."

verses.text: “Enoch walked with God, and then he disappeared because God took him away.”

events.title: Methuselah to Noah
events.detail: The genealogy continues through Methuselah — the longest-lived man in the record — to Lamech, who names his son Noah in hope of relief from the ground's curse.

eras.label: Era Six · Genesis 6
eras.name: The Nephilim, and the Coming Flood
eras.dates: Mysterious unions between "the sons of God" and human women coincide with humanity's wickedness reaching a breaking point, and God resolves to wipe out every living thing except one righteous family.

events.title: "Every Inclination… Was Only Evil"
events.detail: The enigmatic Nephilim appear as the sons of God take human wives, and the LORD, seeing humanity's total moral corruption, regrets creating them and resolves to wipe them out — except for Noah, who "found favor in the sight of the LORD."

verses.text: “The LORD [Yahweh] saw that the wickedness of humankind had become great on the earth. Every inclination of the thoughts of their minds was only evil all the time. The LORD [Yahweh] regretted that he had made humankind on the earth, and he was highly offended.”

events.title: Building the Ark
events.detail: God gives Noah — described as "blameless among his contemporaries" — detailed instructions for building the ark and confirms a covenant to preserve him, his family, and pairs of every living creature.

verses.text: “This is the account of Noah. Noah was a godly man; he was blameless among his contemporaries. He walked with God [Elohim].”

eras.label: Era Seven · Genesis 7
eras.name: Entering the Ark
eras.dates: Noah's obedience is total and unremarkable in its telling — he simply does everything God commands — before the fountains of the deep burst open and the waters rise until every high mountain disappears.

events.title: Seven Pairs, and Seven Days' Warning
events.detail: The LORD gives Noah a week's notice and instructs him to bring seven pairs of clean animals and one pair of unclean ones, and Noah "did all that the LORD commanded him."

events.title: The Flood Covers the Earth
events.detail: On a specific date, all the fountains of the deep burst open and it rains forty days and nights; the waters rise more than twenty feet above the highest mountains, and every living thing outside the ark dies.

verses.text: “So the LORD [Yahweh] destroyed every living thing that was on the surface of the ground… They were wiped off the earth. Only Noah and those who were with him in the ark survived.”

eras.label: Era Eight · Genesis 8
eras.name: The Flood Recedes
eras.dates: God "remembers" Noah, and the waters slowly withdraw — marked by a raven that never returns and a dove that comes back first empty-handed, then bearing an olive leaf, then not at all.

events.title: The Raven and the Dove
events.detail: God causes a wind to blow and the waters recede over months; Noah sends out a raven and then a dove three times, the second return bringing a fresh olive leaf as proof the earth was drying.

verses.text: “God remembered Noah and all the wild animals and domestic animals that were with him in the ark. God caused a wind to blow over the earth and the waters receded.”

events.title: "I Will Never Again Curse the Ground"
events.detail: Noah leaves the ark, builds an altar, and offers sacrifices; the LORD smells the offering and privately resolves never again to destroy every living thing, promising that seasons and day and night will continue without ceasing.

verses.text: “The LORD [Yahweh] smelled the soothing aroma and said to himself, ‘I will never again curse the ground because of humankind… While the earth continues to exist, planting time and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, and day and night will not cease.’”

eras.label: Era Nine · Genesis 9
eras.name: The Noahic Covenant, and Noah's Drunkenness
eras.dates: God formally covenants never again to destroy the earth by flood, sealing the promise with the rainbow — before the book's first post-flood generation stumbles into its own family scandal.

events.title: The Rainbow Covenant
events.detail: God blesses Noah's family, permits eating meat for the first time (with its blood forbidden), and establishes an everlasting covenant never again to destroy the earth by flood, giving the rainbow as its permanent sign.

verses.text: “Whoever sheds human blood, by other humans must his blood be shed; for in God's [Elohim] image God [Elohim] has made humankind.”

events.title: Noah's Vineyard, and Canaan Cursed
events.detail: Noah gets drunk on wine from his own vineyard and is seen naked by his son Ham, who tells his brothers rather than covering him; Noah's resulting curse falls not on Ham directly but on Ham's son Canaan.

verses.text: “So he said, ‘Cursed be Canaan! The lowest of slaves he will be to his brothers.’ He also said, ‘Worthy of praise is the LORD [Yahweh], the God [Elohim] of Shem! May Canaan be the slave of Shem!’”

eras.label: Era Ten · Genesis 10
eras.name: The Table of Nations
eras.dates: A sweeping genealogy accounts for every nation known to ancient Israel as descending from Noah's three sons — Japheth, Ham, and Shem — including the notable warrior-king Nimrod.

events.title: Seventy Nations From Three Sons
events.detail: The descendants of Japheth, Ham, and Shem are traced by name, family, language, and territory, including Nimrod, "a mighty hunter before the LORD," whose kingdom included Babel — setting up the very next chapter's story.

verses.text: “Cush was the father of Nimrod; he began to be a valiant warrior on the earth. He was a mighty hunter before the LORD [Yahweh].”

eras.label: Era Eleven · Genesis 11
eras.name: The Tower of Babel
eras.dates: A unified humanity's ambition to "make a name for ourselves" with a tower reaching the heavens is undone by God's confusion of their language — the very event that gives Babel its name.

events.title: "Let's Build a Tower With Its Top in the Heavens"
events.detail: A single-language humanity builds a city and tower to avoid being scattered, but the LORD confuses their language and scatters them across the earth anyway — the reason the place is called Babel.

verses.text: “Its name was called Babel — because there the LORD [Yahweh] confused the language of the entire world, and from there the LORD [Yahweh] scattered them across the face of the entire earth.”

events.title: Shem's Line to Abram
events.detail: The genealogy from Shem narrows through Arphaxad, Eber, and Peleg down to Terah and his son Abram, who sets out from Ur of the Chaldeans with his father, nephew Lot, and wife Sarai, the childless one.

eras.label: Era Twelve · Genesis 12
eras.name: Abram's Call, and a Detour to Egypt
eras.dates: God's call to Abram launches the central story of the rest of the book — a promise of nationhood and blessing — immediately tested when a famine drives Abram to Egypt and a lie about Sarai nearly costs him everything.

events.title: "I Will Make You Into a Great Nation"
events.detail: The LORD calls Abram to leave his country for a land he has not yet seen, promising to make him a great nation and a source of blessing for all the earth's families; Abram obeys, builds altars along the way, and worships the LORD by name.

verses.text: “The LORD [Yahweh] said to Abram, ‘Go out from your country… to the land that I will show you. Then I will make you into a great nation, and I will bless you… so that all the families of the earth may receive blessing through you.’”

events.title: "She Is My Sister" — Abram in Egypt
events.detail: A severe famine drives Abram to Egypt, where fear leads him to pass Sarai off as his sister; Pharaoh takes her into his household until the LORD strikes his house with disease, and Pharaoh sends the couple away once he learns the truth.

eras.label: Era Thirteen · Genesis 13
eras.name: Abram and Lot Separate
eras.dates: Grown too wealthy to share the same land, Abram lets Lot choose first — a generosity that leaves Abram in Canaan and Lot pitching his tents dangerously close to Sodom.

events.title: "Is Not the Whole Land Before You?"
events.detail: To end quarrels between their herdsmen, Abram lets Lot choose his territory first; Lot picks the well-watered Jordan plain near Sodom, and afterward the LORD reaffirms to Abram that all the land he can see will belong to his uncountable descendants.

verses.text: “After Lot had departed, the LORD [Yahweh] said to Abram, ‘Look… I will give all the land that you see to you and your descendants forever. And I will make your descendants like the dust of the earth.’”

eras.label: Era Fourteen · Genesis 14
eras.name: The War of the Kings, and Melchizedek
eras.dates: A coalition war between distant kings sweeps up Lot as a captive, prompting Abram's only military campaign in the book — and a mysterious priest-king who blesses him in the name of God Most High.

events.title: Abram Rescues Lot
events.detail: When a coalition of eastern kings defeats Sodom's alliance and carries off Lot along with the city's plunder, Abram mobilizes 318 trained men, pursues the invaders as far as Damascus, and recovers everyone and everything taken.

events.title: Melchizedek Blesses Abram
events.detail: Melchizedek, king of Salem and priest of God Most High, brings out bread and wine and blesses Abram, who gives him a tenth of everything; Abram then refuses any reward from the king of Sodom so that no one could ever say Sodom made him rich.

verses.text: “He blessed him and said, ‘Blessed be Abram by God [El] Most High, Creator of heaven and earth. Worthy of praise is God [El] Most High, who delivered your enemies into your hand.’”

eras.label: Era Fifteen · Genesis 15
eras.name: The Covenant of the Pieces
eras.dates: God answers Abram's doubt about an heir with a promise counted in stars, and seals a land covenant with a strange nighttime ritual — a smoking firepot and flaming torch passing alone between the halves of sacrificed animals.

events.title: "Your Descendants Will Be as the Stars"
events.detail: Abram voices his frustration that his heir would be a servant rather than his own child; God promises descendants as countless as the stars, and Abram's belief is credited to him as righteousness.

verses.text: “Abram believed the LORD [Yahweh], and the LORD [Yahweh] credited it as righteousness to him.”

events.title: The Smoking Firepot Between the Pieces
events.detail: God has Abram cut animals in half and arrange them, then puts him into a deep sleep to foretell 400 years of slavery for his descendants before deliverance; a smoking firepot and flaming torch — representing God alone, not Abram — pass between the pieces to seal the covenant.

verses.text: “The LORD said to Abram, ‘Know for certain that your descendants will be strangers in a foreign country. They will be enslaved and oppressed for 400 years.’”

eras.label: Era Sixteen · Genesis 16
eras.name: Hagar and Ishmael
eras.dates: Sarai's plan to build a family through her servant Hagar backfires into rivalry and flight, until the angel of the LORD meets Hagar in the wilderness and gives Ishmael his name.

events.title: "You Are the God Who Sees Me"
events.detail: Sarai gives her servant Hagar to Abram to bear a child on her behalf, but Hagar's contempt for her once pregnant leads to harsh treatment and flight; the angel of the LORD finds Hagar at a wilderness spring, promises to multiply her descendants, and instructs her to name her son Ishmael, "for the LORD has heard your painful groans."

verses.text: “Hagar named the LORD [Yahweh] who spoke to her, ‘You are the God [El] who sees me,’ for she said, ‘Here I have seen one who sees me!’”

eras.label: Era Seventeen · Genesis 17
eras.name: The Covenant of Circumcision
eras.dates: At ninety-nine, Abram receives new names for himself and Sarai along with the sign that will mark his covenant in the flesh of every male descendant — circumcision, carried out that very day.

events.title: Abram Becomes Abraham
events.detail: God renames Abram "Abraham" — father of a multitude of nations — confirms the covenant as perpetual, and institutes circumcision on the eighth day as its permanent physical sign for every male descendant.

verses.text: “As for me, this is my covenant with you: You will be the father of a multitude of nations. No longer will your name be Abram. Instead, your name will be Abraham because I will make you the father of a multitude of nations.”

events.title: Sarah's New Name, and Isaac Promised
events.detail: Sarai is renamed Sarah and promised a son named Isaac within the year despite Abraham's disbelieving laughter; Ishmael is also blessed with a promise of twelve princes, and Abraham circumcises every male in his household that same day.

verses.text: “God said, ‘No, Sarah your wife is going to bear you a son, and you will name him Isaac. I will confirm my covenant with him as a perpetual covenant for his descendants after him.’”

eras.label: Era Eighteen · Genesis 18
eras.name: Three Visitors, and Abraham's Intercession
eras.dates: Three mysterious visitors confirm Sarah's coming pregnancy despite her private, disbelieving laugh, before Abraham boldly bargains the LORD down from fifty righteous people to just ten to spare Sodom.

events.title: "Is Anything Impossible for the LORD?"
events.detail: Abraham hosts three visitors at Mamre with lavish hospitality; when one promises Sarah a son within the year, she laughs privately in disbelief, and the LORD calls her out on it directly.

verses.text: “Is anything impossible for the LORD [Yahweh]? I will return to you when the season comes round again and Sarah will have a son.”

events.title: Bargaining Down to Ten Righteous People
events.detail: Learning of Sodom's coming judgment, Abraham appeals to God's justice and negotiates the threshold for sparing the city down from fifty righteous people to just ten, never quite daring to ask if none can be found.

verses.text: “Far be it from you to do such a thing — to kill the godly with the wicked, treating the godly and the wicked alike! Far be it from you! Will not the judge of the whole earth do what is right?”

eras.label: Era Nineteen · Genesis 19
eras.name: Sodom and Gomorrah
eras.dates: Ten righteous people cannot be found, and Lot barely escapes the cities' destruction — his wife turned to salt for looking back, and his daughters resorting to a desperate, disturbing scheme once safely in the hills.

events.title: The Men of Sodom Surround Lot's House
events.detail: The two angels are met at Sodom's gate by Lot, whose hospitality is repaid when the city's men surround his house demanding to assault his guests; the angels strike the mob blind and warn Lot to gather his family and flee the coming destruction.

events.title: Fire and Sulfur, and a Pillar of Salt
events.detail: Lot hesitates until the angels physically drag his family out of the city; as they flee, the LORD rains sulfur and fire on Sodom and Gomorrah, and Lot's wife, looking back, is turned into a pillar of salt.

verses.text: “The LORD [Yahweh] rained down sulfur and fire on Sodom and Gomorrah… But Lot's wife looked back longingly and was turned into a pillar of salt.”

events.title: Lot's Daughters
events.detail: Believing no husbands remain for them, Lot's daughters get their father drunk on consecutive nights and conceive children by him, becoming the ancestors of the Moabites and Ammonites.

eras.label: Era Twenty · Genesis 20
eras.name: Abraham and Abimelech
eras.dates: Abraham repeats his old fear-driven lie about Sarah with a second foreign king, but this time God intervenes in a dream before anything happens, protecting Abimelech's innocence and Sarah's honor alike.

events.title: "You Are as Good as Dead"
events.detail: Abraham again claims Sarah is his sister out of fear, and Abimelech takes her — but God appears to Abimelech in a dream before he touches her, warning him of certain death, and Abimelech returns Sarah along with generous compensation once the truth comes out.

verses.text: “In the dream God replied to him, ‘Yes, I know that you have done this with a clear conscience. That is why I have kept you from sinning against me and why I did not allow you to touch her.’”

eras.label: Era Twenty-One · Genesis 21
eras.name: Isaac Born; Hagar and Ishmael Sent Away
eras.dates: The long-promised son finally arrives, and his birth triggers Ishmael's expulsion into the wilderness — where God again meets Hagar, this time opening her eyes to a well that saves her dying son's life.

events.title: "God Has Made Me Laugh"
events.detail: Sarah bears Isaac exactly as the LORD had promised, and her earlier private laugh of disbelief becomes public joy — "everyone who hears about this will laugh with me."

verses.text: “The LORD [Yahweh] visited Sarah just as he had said he would and did for Sarah what he had promised. So Sarah became pregnant and bore Abraham a son in his old age at the appointed time that God [Elohim] had told him.”

events.title: Hagar and Ishmael in the Wilderness
events.detail: Sarah demands Hagar and Ishmael be banished after seeing Ishmael mocking at Isaac's weaning feast; sent into the wilderness with dwindling supplies, Hagar despairs of her son's life until God opens her eyes to see a well of water.

verses.text: “God heard the boy's voice. The angel of God called to Hagar from heaven and asked her, ‘What is the matter, Hagar? Don't be afraid, for God has heard the boy's voice right where he is crying. Get up! Help the boy up… for I will make him into a great nation.’”

events.title: A Treaty at Beer Sheba
events.detail: Abimelech seeks a formal treaty with Abraham, who uses the occasion to settle a dispute over a well; the two make peace at Beer Sheba, and Abraham worships the LORD there as "the eternal God."

eras.label: Era Twenty-Two · Genesis 22
eras.name: The Binding of Isaac
eras.dates: God's most severe test of Abraham — sacrifice the promised son himself — is stopped at the last possible moment by an angel's voice, revealing a ram already caught in the thicket as the real offering all along.

events.title: "God Will Provide for Himself the Lamb"
events.detail: God tests Abraham by commanding him to sacrifice Isaac; Abraham obeys to the point of raising the knife before the angel of the LORD stops him, and a ram caught in a nearby thicket becomes the actual sacrifice — giving the place its name, "The LORD Provides."

verses.text: “Do not harm the boy! Do not do anything to him, for now I know that you fear God [Elohim] because you did not withhold your son, your only son, from me.”
“Abraham called the name of that place ‘The LORD [Yahweh] provides.’ It is said to this day, ‘In the mountain of the LORD [Yahweh] provision will be made.’”

events.title: The Oath Renewed, and News of Nahor's Family
events.detail: The angel of the LORD renews the covenant promise with a solemn oath because Abraham did not withhold his only son, and news arrives of children born to Abraham's brother Nahor, including Rebekah — the woman who will become Isaac's wife.

verses.text: “I solemnly swear by my own name, decrees the LORD [Yahweh], that because you have done this and have not withheld your son, your only son, I will indeed bless you, and I will greatly multiply your descendants.”

eras.label: Era Twenty-Three · Genesis 23
eras.name: Sarah's Death and Burial
eras.dates: Abraham's grief over Sarah leads to a careful, fully-documented land purchase — the cave of Machpelah — establishing the first piece of the promised land Abraham's family would actually own outright.

events.title: The Cave of Machpelah
events.detail: After Sarah's death, Abraham negotiates publicly and insistently to pay full price for the cave of Machpelah as a burial site, refusing Ephron's offer to simply give it to him — securing legal, undisputed ownership of the first parcel of the promised land.

verses.text: “Abraham agreed to Ephron's price and weighed out for him the price that Ephron had quoted… 400 pieces of silver, according to the standard measurement at the time.”

eras.label: Era Twenty-Four · Genesis 24
eras.name: A Wife for Isaac
eras.dates: The book's longest single chapter follows Abraham's servant on a detailed, prayer-guided mission back to Abraham's homeland, where a young woman's spontaneous generosity at a well identifies her as Isaac's God-chosen bride.

events.title: A Prayer at the Well
events.detail: Abraham sends his senior servant, under solemn oath, to find a wife for Isaac from his own relatives rather than the Canaanites; the servant prays for a specific sign — a woman who offers to water his camels unprompted — and Rebekah appears and does exactly that before he finishes praying.

verses.text: “He prayed, ‘O LORD [Yahweh], God [Elohim] of my master Abraham, guide me today… May the one you have chosen for your servant Isaac reply, “Drink, and I'll give your camels water too.” In this way I will know that you have been faithful to my master.’”

events.title: The Servant's Account to Laban and the Family
events.detail: Rebekah's brother Laban welcomes the servant, who retells the entire well encounter in detail before the family, framing it explicitly as evidence of the LORD's guidance rather than mere coincidence.

events.title: "I Want to Go" — Rebekah Consents
events.detail: Laban and Bethuel recognize the match as "the LORD's doing" and let Rebekah herself decide; she agrees immediately, and Isaac, meeting her in the field, takes her as his wife and finds comfort in her after his mother's death.

verses.text: “Isaac brought Rebekah into his mother Sarah's tent. He took her as his wife and loved her. So Isaac was comforted after his mother's death.”

eras.label: Era Twenty-Five · Genesis 25
eras.name: Abraham's Death; Esau's Birthright Sold
eras.dates: Abraham dies at a full old age and is buried beside Sarah by both his sons together, and the narrative's focus shifts decisively to the next generation — twins struggling in the womb, and a hungry Esau trading his birthright for a bowl of stew.

events.title: Abraham's Death, and Ishmael's Line
events.detail: Abraham dies at 175 and is buried by Isaac and Ishmael together in the cave of Machpelah; Ishmael's own twelve sons become tribal princes before he too dies, closing out the Abraham narrative.

verses.text: “Abraham breathed his last and died at a good old age, an old man who had lived a full life. He joined his ancestors.”

events.title: "The Older Will Serve the Younger" — the Birthright Sold
events.detail: Rebekah's difficult twin pregnancy prompts a divine oracle that the younger will rule the older; Esau, the hairy firstborn hunter, later trades his entire birthright to Jacob for a bowl of lentil stew in a moment of hunger, and the narrator notes flatly that Esau "despised his birthright."

verses.text: “The LORD [Yahweh] said to her, ‘Two nations are in your womb, and two peoples will be separated from within you. One people will be stronger than the other, and the older will serve the younger.’”

eras.label: Era Twenty-Six · Genesis 26
eras.name: Isaac Among the Philistines
eras.dates: Isaac's own story largely retraces his father's — a lie about his wife to a foreign king, disputes over wells, and a covenant of peace — proving the family pattern runs deeper than any one generation.

events.title: "She Is My Sister" — Isaac Repeats His Father's Lie
events.detail: Isaac repeats Abraham's old strategy, calling Rebekah his sister out of fear, until Abimelech catches him caressing her and realizes the truth; Isaac's harvests and flocks grow so prosperous that the Philistines grow jealous and stop up his father's old wells.

verses.text: “When Isaac planted in that land, he reaped in the same year a hundred times what he had sown, because the LORD [Yahweh] blessed him.”

events.title: Wells Named for Strife, Then Room to Prosper
events.detail: Isaac's servants dig wells that repeatedly draw quarrels until one, Rehoboth, finally goes uncontested; Abimelech seeks a peace treaty once he sees the LORD's evident blessing on Isaac, and the chapter closes noting Esau's Hittite wives caused his parents "great anxiety."

verses.text: “They replied, ‘We could plainly see that the LORD [Yahweh] is with you. So we decided there should be a pact between us.’”

eras.label: Era Twenty-Seven · Genesis 27
eras.name: Jacob Steals Esau's Blessing
eras.dates: Rebekah's scheme to secure Isaac's blessing for Jacob instead of Esau succeeds through deception and disguise, permanently fracturing the brothers and forcing Jacob to flee for his life.

events.title: "The Voice Is Jacob's, but the Hands Are Esau's"
events.detail: Rebekah dresses Jacob in Esau's clothes and goat skins to fool blind Isaac into giving him the firstborn's blessing instead of Esau — a blessing of abundance and authority over his brothers, secured through deliberate deception.

verses.text: “My son smells like the scent of an open field which the LORD [Yahweh] has blessed. May God [Elohim] give you the dew of the sky and the richness of the earth… You will be lord over your brothers.”

events.title: Esau's Bitter Cry, and Jacob's Flight
events.detail: Esau's anguished discovery of the deception — "Bless me too, my father!" — earns only a lesser blessing of servitude and eventual freedom; Esau vows to kill Jacob once their father dies, prompting Rebekah to send Jacob away to her brother Laban in Haran.

verses.text: “When Esau heard his father's words, he wailed loudly and bitterly. He said to his father, ‘Bless me too, my father!’”

eras.label: Era Twenty-Eight · Genesis 28
eras.name: Jacob's Ladder at Bethel
eras.dates: Fleeing alone into the wilderness, Jacob receives the covenant promise in a dream of a stairway reaching heaven — and responds not with faith but with a conditional bargain.

events.title: Isaac Sends Jacob Off With a Blessing
events.detail: Isaac formally blesses Jacob and sends him to Paddan Aram to find a wife among Laban's daughters rather than the local Canaanites; seeing this, Esau — already aware his Canaanite wives displease his father — marries a daughter of Ishmael as well.

events.title: "Surely the LORD Is in This Place"
events.detail: Jacob dreams of a stairway between earth and heaven with angels ascending and descending, and the LORD renews the Abrahamic covenant promise directly to him; Jacob wakes in awe, consecrates the stone he slept on, and vows a tenth of everything back to God — but only "if" God protects and provides for him.

verses.text: “There! The LORD [Yahweh] was standing on it and he said, ‘I am the LORD [Yahweh], the God [Elohim] of Abraham your father and the God [Elohim] of Isaac. The land which you are lying on, I will give it to you and to your offspring.’”
“Jacob awoke from his sleep and said, ‘Truly the LORD [Yahweh] is in this place, and I did not realize it!’”

eras.label: Era Twenty-Nine · Genesis 29
eras.name: Jacob Serves Laban for Leah and Rachel
eras.dates: The deceiver becomes the deceived when Laban substitutes Leah for Rachel on the wedding night, trapping Jacob into fourteen years of labor for the wife he actually wanted.

events.title: Jacob Meets Rachel at the Well
events.detail: Jacob arrives in Haran and meets Rachel at the same well tradition, rolling the stone off it himself before weeping and kissing her — she is his cousin, Laban's daughter.

events.title: "Why Have You Tricked Me?" — Leah Substituted for Rachel
events.detail: Jacob agrees to work seven years for Rachel, but Laban substitutes her older sister Leah on the wedding night under cover of darkness; Jacob must work seven additional years for Rachel as well, receiving her only a week later.

verses.text: “In the morning Jacob discovered it was Leah! So Jacob said to Laban, ‘What in the world have you done to me? Didn't I work for you in exchange for Rachel? Why have you tricked me?’”

events.title: Leah's First Four Sons
events.detail: Seeing Leah unloved, the LORD opens her womb while Rachel remains childless; Leah bears Reuben, Simeon, Levi, and Judah, naming each son after her own hope for her husband's affection.

verses.text: “When the LORD [Yahweh] saw that Leah was unloved, he enabled her to become pregnant while Rachel remained childless.”

eras.label: Era Thirty · Genesis 30
eras.name: Jacob's Growing Family and Flocks
eras.dates: A fertility rivalry between sisters, fought through servant-wives and mandrakes, produces most of the twelve tribes of Israel — while a clever breeding scheme lets Jacob grow wealthy at Laban's expense.

events.title: The Sister Rivalry, and Joseph's Birth
events.detail: Rachel's desperate jealousy leads to children through her servant Bilhah and Leah's through her servant Zilpah, then a mandrake-for-a-night trade produces two more sons for Leah, until God finally opens Rachel's own womb for Joseph.

verses.text: “God took note of Rachel. He paid attention to her and enabled her to become pregnant. She became pregnant and gave birth to a son. Then she said, ‘God has taken away my shame.’”

events.title: Streaked Branches and a Prosperous Flock
events.detail: Jacob negotiates to keep only the speckled and streaked animals from Laban's flock as wages, then uses peeled branches at the watering troughs to selectively breed the strongest animals into his own flock, becoming "extremely prosperous."

eras.label: Era Thirty-One · Genesis 31
eras.name: Jacob Flees Laban
eras.dates: Sensing Laban's growing hostility, Jacob leaves in secret with his wives, children, and flocks — only for Rachel to steal her father's household idols on the way out, nearly triggering disaster when Laban catches up. (Hebrew verse 55 is numbered as most English Bibles' 32:1.)

events.title: Jacob Leaves Secretly
events.detail: With Laban's sons growing resentful and Laban's own attitude cooling, the LORD tells Jacob to return home; Jacob slips away without telling Laban, and Rachel secretly steals her father's household idols on the way out.

verses.text: “The LORD [Yahweh] said to Jacob, ‘Return to the land of your fathers and to your relatives. I will be with you.’”

events.title: Laban's Pursuit, and the Search for the Idols
events.detail: Laban pursues Jacob for seven days and confronts him, but God had already warned Laban in a dream not to harm Jacob; a thorough search for the stolen idols fails because Rachel sits on them and claims to be menstruating, and Jacob finally vents twenty years of grievances at his father-in-law.

verses.text: “God came to Laban the Aramean in a dream at night and warned him, ‘Be careful that you neither bless nor curse Jacob.’”

events.title: A Covenant of Stones at Galeed
events.detail: Jacob and Laban formalize a peace treaty marked by a pile of stones neither will cross to harm the other, invoking the God of both their fathers as witness before parting ways for good. (Verse 55 numbered as most English Bibles' 32:1.)

eras.label: Era Thirty-Two · Genesis 32
eras.name: Wrestling With God
eras.dates: Terrified of Esau's approach with four hundred men, Jacob sends ahead lavish gifts, prays desperately, and then spends a solitary night wrestling an unnamed man who dislocates his hip and renames him Israel. (Hebrew verse 1 corresponds to most English Bibles' 31:55.)

events.title: Gifts Sent Ahead to Appease Esau
events.detail: Word that Esau approaches with four hundred men terrifies Jacob into dividing his camp for safety, praying for rescue while citing God's own promises back to him, and sending waves of livestock ahead as an appeasing gift.

verses.text: “Jacob prayed, ‘O God of my father Abraham, God of my father Isaac, O LORD [Yahweh], you said to me, “Return to your land and to your relatives and I will make you prosper.” I am not worthy of all the faithful love you have shown your servant.’”

events.title: "Your Name Will Be Israel"
events.detail: Left alone at the Jabbok, Jacob wrestles a man until daybreak, refusing to let go without a blessing even after his hip is dislocated; the man renames him Israel — "you have fought with God and with men and have prevailed" — and Jacob names the place Peniel.

verses.text: “No longer will your name be Jacob,” the man told him, “but Israel, because you have fought with God [Elohim] and with men and have prevailed.”
“Jacob named the place Peniel, explaining, ‘Certainly I have seen God face to face and have survived.’”

eras.label: Era Thirty-Three · Genesis 33
eras.name: Reconciliation With Esau
eras.dates: The confrontation Jacob dreaded for two chapters resolves in an embrace rather than violence, as Esau runs to meet him with open arms instead of the four hundred men's worth of vengeance Jacob had feared.

events.title: "It Is as If I Have Seen the Face of God"
events.detail: Esau runs to Jacob, embraces him, and weeps rather than attacking; Jacob insists Esau accept his gift, comparing the reception to seeing God's own face, before the brothers part peacefully and Jacob settles near Shechem.

verses.text: “If I have found favor in your sight, accept my gift from my hand. Now that I have seen your face and you have accepted me, it is as if I have seen the face of God [Elohim].”

eras.label: Era Thirty-Four · Genesis 34
eras.name: The Rape of Dinah
eras.dates: Shechem's assault on Jacob's daughter Dinah triggers a brutal, deceitful revenge from her brothers Simeon and Levi — circumcision offered in bad faith, followed by a massacre while the men of the city are still recovering.

events.title: Simeon and Levi's Deceitful Revenge
events.detail: After Shechem assaults Dinah and then wants to marry her, Jacob's sons demand the whole city be circumcised as a condition — then Simeon and Levi exploit the men's incapacitation three days later to slaughter every male and plunder the city, appalling Jacob but leaving them unrepentant: "Should he treat our sister like a common prostitute?"

verses.text: “Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, ‘You have brought ruin on me… I am few in number; they will join forces against me and attack me.’ But Simeon and Levi replied, ‘Should he treat our sister like a common prostitute?’”

eras.label: Era Thirty-Five · Genesis 35
eras.name: Return to Bethel; Rachel's Death
eras.dates: God renews both Jacob's name-change and the covenant promise at Bethel, but the joy is cut short almost immediately by Rachel's death in childbirth on the road to Bethlehem.

events.title: God Renews the Covenant at Bethel
events.detail: Jacob's household purges its foreign idols and returns to Bethel, where God confirms the name change to Israel and repeats the covenant promise of nationhood and land first given to Abraham.

verses.text: “God said to him, ‘Your name is Jacob, but your name will no longer be called Jacob; Israel will be your name.’ So God named him Israel. Then God said to him, ‘I am God Almighty [El Shaddai]. Be fruitful and multiply!’”

events.title: Rachel Dies Bearing Benjamin
events.detail: Rachel dies in hard labor delivering Benjamin, naming him with her dying breath before Jacob renames him; Reuben's affair with his father's concubine Bilhah is noted in passing, and the chapter closes with Isaac's death and burial by both Esau and Jacob.

verses.text: “With her dying breath, she named him Ben Oni. But his father called him Benjamin instead. So Rachel died and was buried on the way to Ephrath.”

eras.label: Era Thirty-Six · Genesis 36
eras.name: Esau's Descendants
eras.dates: A genealogy tracks Esau's line into the nation of Edom, complete with its own kings and chiefs — a people who will keep resurfacing throughout the rest of Israel's story as both kin and rival.

events.title: The Line of Esau, Father of the Edomites
events.detail: Esau's wives, sons, and grandsons are traced in detail through the Horite clans already living in Seir and the kings who eventually ruled Edom "before any king ruled over the Israelites" — a genealogy that will matter later when Edom and Israel collide repeatedly.

eras.label: Era Thirty-Seven · Genesis 37
eras.name: Joseph Sold Into Slavery
eras.dates: Favoritism, tattling, and two grandiose dreams turn Joseph's brothers' jealousy murderous, until Judah's suggestion to sell him instead spares his life — at the cost of decades of separation from his father.

events.title: Two Dreams of Dominance
events.detail: Joseph's special tunic and his dreams of his family's sheaves and celestial bodies bowing down to him deepen his brothers' hatred, though his father Jacob "kept in mind" what the dreams might mean.

verses.text: “He had another dream, and told it to his brothers. ‘The sun, the moon, and eleven stars were bowing down to me.’ When he told his father… his father rebuked him, saying, ‘Will I, your mother, and your brothers really come and bow down to you?’”

events.title: Sold to the Ishmaelites
events.detail: Joseph's brothers plot to kill him at Dothan, but Reuben's intervention and Judah's suggestion result in his sale to passing traders instead; his bloodied tunic convinces Jacob a wild animal killed him, and Jacob refuses to be consoled.

verses.text: “Judah said to his brothers, ‘What profit is there if we kill our brother… Come, let's sell him to the Ishmaelites.’ His brothers agreed… and sold him to the Ishmaelites for 20 pieces of silver.”

eras.label: Era Thirty-Eight · Genesis 38
eras.name: Judah and Tamar
eras.dates: A story seemingly unrelated to Joseph interrupts his narrative — Judah's own moral failures with his daughter-in-law Tamar, whose determined pursuit of justice exposes Judah's hypocrisy and produces the ancestor of David's line.

events.title: "She Is More Righteous Than I"
events.detail: After Judah's first two sons die for their wickedness and he withholds his third from Tamar, she disguises herself as a prostitute to secure an heir through Judah himself; when he threatens to have her burned for apparent prostitution, her proof — his own seal, cord, and staff — forces Judah to admit "she is more upright than I am."

verses.text: “Judah recognized them and said, ‘She is more upright than I am, because I wouldn't give her to Shelah my son.’ He was not physically intimate with her again.”

eras.label: Era Thirty-Nine · Genesis 39
eras.name: Joseph and Potiphar's Wife
eras.dates: Sold into an Egyptian household, Joseph rises through sheer competence and the LORD's evident blessing — only to be falsely accused and imprisoned after refusing his master's wife's repeated advances.

events.title: "How Could I Sin Against God?"
events.detail: The LORD's blessing on everything Joseph does earns him complete authority over Potiphar's household; when Potiphar's wife propositions him repeatedly, he refuses on the explicit grounds that it would be a sin against God, eventually fleeing and leaving his garment in her grasping hand.

verses.text: “There is no one greater in this household than I am. He has withheld nothing from me except you because you are his wife. So how could I do such a great evil and sin against God [Elohim]?”

events.title: False Accusation and Prison
events.detail: Potiphar's wife uses Joseph's abandoned garment as false evidence of assault, and Joseph is imprisoned despite his innocence; even there, the narrative insists twice that "the LORD was with Joseph," who soon finds favor with the prison warden.

verses.text: “The LORD [Yahweh] was with Joseph and showed him kindness. He granted him favor in the sight of the prison warden.”

eras.label: Era Forty · Genesis 40
eras.name: The Cupbearer and the Baker
eras.dates: Two fellow prisoners' dreams give Joseph his first chance to demonstrate that dream interpretation belongs to God — accurately predicting one man's restoration and the other's execution within three days.

events.title: "Don't Interpretations Belong to God?"
events.detail: Pharaoh's imprisoned cupbearer and baker each have a troubling dream; Joseph interprets both accurately — restoration for the cupbearer, execution for the baker, both within three days — but asks to be remembered once the cupbearer is free, a request the cupbearer promptly forgets.

verses.text: “They told him, ‘We both had dreams, but there is no one to interpret them.’ Joseph responded, ‘Don't interpretations belong to God [Elohim]? Tell them to me.’”

eras.label: Era Forty-One · Genesis 41
eras.name: Joseph Interprets Pharaoh's Dreams
eras.dates: Two years after being forgotten, Joseph is suddenly summoned from prison to interpret Pharaoh's own troubling dreams — seven fat cows devoured by seven lean ones — and is elevated to second-in-command of all Egypt within the same chapter.

events.title: Seven Years of Plenty, Seven Years of Famine
events.detail: Pharaoh's twin dreams of fat and lean cattle and grain stump every Egyptian wise man until the cupbearer finally remembers Joseph; Joseph interprets both dreams as seven years of abundance followed by seven of severe famine, and proposes a systematic plan to store surplus grain.

verses.text: “Joseph replied to Pharaoh, ‘It is not within my power, but God will speak concerning the welfare of Pharaoh.’”
“The dream was repeated to Pharaoh because the matter has been decreed by God, and God will make it happen soon.”

events.title: Joseph Elevated Over All Egypt
events.detail: Pharaoh recognizes the Spirit of God in Joseph and places him in charge of all Egypt on the spot; Joseph marries, fathers Manasseh and Ephraim, and manages the abundance so effectively that when famine strikes as predicted, people from every country come to Egypt to buy grain from him.

verses.text: “Pharaoh said to Joseph, ‘Because God has enabled you to know all this, there is no one as wise and discerning as you are! You will oversee my household, and all my people will submit to your commands.’”

eras.label: Era Forty-Two · Genesis 42
eras.name: The Brothers' First Journey to Egypt
eras.dates: Famine drives Joseph's own brothers, unrecognizing, straight into his power; he tests them with accusations of spying and detains Simeon, all while his identity remains hidden and his emotions nearly break through.

events.title: Ten Brothers, and an Unrecognized Ruler
events.detail: Ten of Joseph's brothers come to buy grain and bow before him without recognizing him; Joseph accuses them of spying, imprisons Simeon as collateral, and demands they bring Benjamin — all while secretly weeping over their guilt-stricken conversation about how they once ignored Joseph's own pleas.

verses.text: “They said to one another, ‘Surely we're being punished because of our brother, because we saw how distressed he was when he cried to us for mercy, but we refused to listen.’ Reuben said to them, ‘Didn't I say to you, “Don't sin against the boy”?’”

eras.label: Era Forty-Three · Genesis 43
eras.name: The Second Journey; Benjamin Goes Down
eras.dates: Desperate for more grain and out of options, Jacob finally releases Benjamin into Judah's personal guarantee, and the brothers return to a surprisingly warm reception — Joseph barely composing himself before their eyes.

events.title: Judah Guarantees Benjamin's Safety
events.detail: With the famine still severe, Judah personally pledges to bear the blame forever if Benjamin does not return safely, finally persuading Jacob to release him along with gifts and double the money for Joseph.

verses.text: “I myself pledge security for him; you may hold me liable. If I do not bring him back to you and place him here before you, I will bear the blame before you all my life.”

events.title: A Feast, and Benjamin's Five-Fold Portion
events.detail: Joseph, overcome at the sight of his mother's other son Benjamin, hosts the brothers at a feast where Benjamin's portion is mysteriously five times larger than anyone else's — a pointed test of whether the brothers still resent favoritism shown to Rachel's sons.

verses.text: “He gave them portions of the food set before him, but the portion for Benjamin was five times greater than the portions for any of the others.”

eras.label: Era Forty-Four · Genesis 44
eras.name: The Silver Cup
eras.dates: Joseph's planted cup in Benjamin's sack sets up the story's real turning point — Judah's impassioned plea to take Benjamin's place as a slave rather than break his father's heart a second time.

events.title: "Let Your Servant Remain Instead of the Boy"
events.detail: Joseph frames Benjamin for stealing his divination cup and demands he stay behind as a slave; Judah — the same brother who once suggested selling Joseph — delivers an impassioned speech offering himself in Benjamin's place rather than watch their father die of grief a second time.

verses.text: “Please let your servant remain as my lord's slave instead of the boy. As for the boy, let him go back with his brothers. For how can I go back to my father if the boy is not with me? I couldn't bear to see my father's pain.”

eras.label: Era Forty-Five · Genesis 45
eras.name: Joseph Reveals Himself
eras.dates: Judah's speech breaks Joseph completely — he sends every Egyptian attendant out of the room and weeps so loudly that Pharaoh's whole household hears it, before reframing his brothers' betrayal as God's own providence.

events.title: "I Am Joseph… God Sent Me Ahead of You"
events.detail: Overcome and unable to maintain the disguise any longer, Joseph reveals his identity to his stunned brothers, reassuring them that God, not their own malice, was the real force behind his being sold into Egypt — to preserve life through the coming famine.

verses.text: “I am Joseph your brother, whom you sold into Egypt. Now, do not be upset and do not be angry with yourselves because you sold me here, for God sent me ahead of you to preserve life!”

events.title: Pharaoh Invites the Whole Family
events.detail: Pharaoh, delighted by the news, offers Jacob's entire household the best land in Egypt; Jacob, initially too stunned to believe his sons, revives at the sight of the wagons Joseph sent and resolves to see his son before he dies.

verses.text: “When he saw the wagons that Joseph had sent to transport him, their father Jacob's spirit revived. Then Israel said, ‘Enough! My son Joseph is still alive! I will go and see him before I die.’”

eras.label: Era Forty-Six · Genesis 46
eras.name: Jacob's Family Moves to Egypt
eras.dates: God personally confirms the migration to Egypt in a nighttime vision, and a careful genealogical tally counts the seventy people of Jacob's household who make the journey to reunite with Joseph.

events.title: "Do Not Be Afraid to Go Down to Egypt"
events.detail: At Beer Sheba, God confirms in a vision that Jacob should go to Egypt without fear, promising to make his family a great nation there and personally to bring them back one day.

verses.text: “He said, ‘I am God [El], the God of your father. Do not be afraid to go down to Egypt, for I will make you into a great nation there. I will go down with you to Egypt and I myself will certainly bring you back from there.’”

events.title: Seventy Souls Counted
events.detail: A careful genealogical list names all of Jacob's direct descendants who go to Egypt, totaling seventy people once Joseph's two Egyptian-born sons are included.

verses.text: “Counting the two sons of Joseph who were born to him in Egypt, all the people of the household of Jacob who were in Egypt numbered seventy.”

events.title: Reunion in Goshen
events.detail: Joseph rides out to meet his father in Goshen and weeps on his neck for a long time; he coaches his brothers to tell Pharaoh they are shepherds specifically so they can settle in Goshen, since shepherding is "disgusting to the Egyptians."

verses.text: “Joseph harnessed his chariot and went up to meet his father Israel in Goshen. When he met him, he hugged his neck and wept on his neck for quite some time.”

eras.label: Era Forty-Seven · Genesis 47
eras.name: Joseph Settles His Family; Famine Policy
eras.dates: Jacob's family is granted the best land in Egypt while Joseph's famine-relief policy quietly converts the rest of the Egyptian population — land, livestock, and all — into Pharaoh's permanent tenants.

events.title: Jacob Blesses Pharaoh
events.detail: Joseph presents his father and brothers to Pharaoh, who grants them Goshen's best land; the aged Jacob, asked his age, describes his years as "few and painful" compared to his ancestors, then blesses Pharaoh.

verses.text: “Jacob said to Pharaoh, ‘All the years of my travels are 130. All the years of my life have been few and painful; the years of my travels are not as long as those of my ancestors.’”

events.title: Egypt's Land Becomes Pharaoh's
events.detail: As the famine deepens, Egyptians sell first their money, then their livestock, then their land and even themselves into Pharaoh's service in exchange for food — a policy Joseph administers so thoroughly it becomes permanent Egyptian law, except for the priests' land.

verses.text: “Buy us and our land in exchange for food, and we, with our land, will become Pharaoh's slaves… So Joseph bought all the land of Egypt for Pharaoh.”

eras.label: Era Forty-Eight · Genesis 48
eras.name: Jacob Blesses Ephraim and Manasseh
eras.dates: Near death, Jacob deliberately crosses his hands to bless Joseph's younger son over the older — repeating, in his own final act, the exact reversal of birth order that shaped his whole life.

events.title: Crossed Hands, and the Younger Blessed
events.detail: Jacob adopts Joseph's two sons as his own and deliberately crosses his hands to place his right hand — the blessing hand — on the younger Ephraim rather than the firstborn Manasseh, insisting he knows exactly what he is doing despite Joseph's objection.

verses.text: “His father refused and said, ‘I know, my son, I know. He too will become a nation and he too will become great. In spite of this, his younger brother will be even greater and his descendants will become a multitude of nations.’”

eras.label: Era Forty-Nine · Genesis 49
eras.name: Jacob's Blessing on His Twelve Sons
eras.dates: Jacob's dying poetic oracle over each of his twelve sons reads as much prophecy as blessing — Reuben's instability, Simeon and Levi's violence condemned, and Judah singled out for a scepter that will not depart until the ruler it belongs to finally comes.

events.title: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, and Judah's Scepter
events.detail: Jacob's blessing turns to rebuke for Reuben's instability and Simeon and Levi's violent revenge at Shechem, then singles out Judah with royal, messianic language — a scepter that will not depart "until he comes to whom it belongs."

verses.text: “The scepter will not depart from Judah, nor the ruler's staff from between his feet, until he comes to whom it belongs; the nations will obey him.”

events.title: The Remaining Eight Sons, and Joseph's Fruitful Bough
events.detail: Each remaining son receives a distinct poetic image — Dan a snake by the road, Joseph a fruitful bough whose bow remained steady "because of the hands of the Powerful One of Jacob" — closing with the statement that Jacob gave "each of them an appropriate blessing."

verses.text: “His bow will remain steady, and his hands will be skillful; because of the hands of the Powerful One of Jacob… because of the God of your father, who will help you, because of the Sovereign God, who will bless you.”

events.title: Jacob's Final Instructions and Death
events.detail: Jacob instructs his sons to bury him with Abraham, Isaac, and their wives in the cave of Machpelah, then pulls his feet onto the bed, breathes his last, and "went to his people."

eras.label: Era Fifty · Genesis 50
eras.name: Jacob's Burial; Joseph's Death
eras.dates: Genesis closes where it began — with faith stretching beyond a single lifetime: Jacob's honored burial back in Canaan, Joseph's forgiveness of his brothers, and a final instruction to carry his own bones out of Egypt one day.

events.title: A State Funeral for Jacob
events.detail: Joseph has his father embalmed and mourned by all Egypt before leading a massive entourage — including Pharaoh's own officials — back to Canaan to bury Jacob in the cave of Machpelah, exactly as he had sworn to do.

events.title: "You Meant to Harm Me, but God Intended It for Good"
events.detail: Fearing revenge now that Jacob is dead, Joseph's brothers beg forgiveness; Joseph weeps and reassures them with the theological statement that summarizes the entire Joseph narrative — their evil intentions were folded into God's larger purpose to preserve many lives.

verses.text: “Joseph answered them, ‘Don't be afraid. Am I in the place of God? As for you, you meant to harm me, but God intended it for a good purpose, so he could preserve the lives of many people.’”

events.title: "God Will Surely Come to You" — Joseph's Death
events.detail: Joseph lives to see his great-grandchildren before dying at 110, making the sons of Israel swear to carry his bones out of Egypt whenever God brings them back to the land promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob — a promise still unfulfilled as the book closes.

verses.text: “Joseph said to his brothers, ‘I am about to die. But God will surely come to you and lead you up from this land to the land he swore on oath to give to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.’ Joseph made the sons of Israel swear an oath.”
